title: Cluster F — Kremenchuk tail (P0783 Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih vs P1460 Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih): DUPLICATE REFUTED

rows.recommendation: Do NOT fold or delete this row — it is a genuine, separately documented 1986 trunk (Єлець–Кременчук–Кривий Ріг, 1400 mm per uk.wikipedia / 1420 mm on the sheet, both readings consistent with the standard Soviet large-diameter trunk class). Route to Update for two narrower, non-duplication items: (1) OWNERSHIP — the row's Owner field names Gazprom PJSC; the documented line runs from Yelets (Lipetsk Oblast, Russia) through Kursk to Kremenchuk and Kryvyi Rih deep inside Ukraine, so if the row attributes the WHOLE line to Gazprom that is an attribution defect of the same kind already flagged on P1485 (cluster C) — Gazprom owns no Ukrainian section; the Ukrainian portion (the large majority of the corridor) belongs to the state operator (Ukrtransgaz historically, Gas TSO of Ukraine since 2020-01-01), and only a cross-border SPLIT (Russian section only = Gazprom-linked infrastructure) is defensible. (2) LENGTH SCOPE — no source found states a length figure at all for this line (uk.wikipedia gives diameter/pressure/year/route only), so the sheet's 771.00 km cannot be independently confirmed as either a Yelets-to-Kryvyi-Rih total (spanning Russia + Ukraine) or a Ukraine-territory-only figure. Given the row's CountriesOrAreas and the Moldovatransgaz-style caveat already applied elsewhere in this project (Moldovan-territory portions vs line-wide specs), this is worth one further length-provenance check before touching the cell — but it is a sourcing gap to chase, not evidence of a duplicate.
rows.notes: uk.wikipedia 'Єлець — Кременчук — Кривий Ріг' (raw wikitext fetched directly, not just search-summarized): diameter 1400 mm, робочий тиск 7,5 МПа, launched 1986 as part of the Siberia(Yamburg)-to-Balkans supply project via the Yelets hub; explicitly categorized under BOTH 'Газопроводи України' and 'Газопроводи Росії', confirming it is understood as a cross-border line, not a Ukraine-only one. At its Kryvyi-Rih-area endpoint the article states gas could be forwarded on to 'Кременчук — Ананьїв' (=P1485, cluster C) and to 'Шебелинка - Кривий Ріг - Ізмаїл' — i.e. P0783 feeds INTO the Kremenchuk-Ananiv system as a distinct, connected upstream line, exactly the reading already reached independently in kab_achb_evidence.md. Two footnoted citations (utg.ua chronology; adm.rkursk.ru) both archived via web.archive.org — read but not independently re-fetched here (same sources already logged in yelets_family_evidence.md for the sibling cluster). No length figure of any kind appears in the article text. Route-geometry test (route_geometry_findings.md, finding F): the P0783 trace shares only its Dykanka-area and Kryvyi-Rih endpoint NODES with P0775/P1460 — 0 of P1460's 3 vertices and only 1 of P0775's 3 vertices lie within 0.5 km of P0783's own trace, so there is no aggregate/concatenation identity (contrast the Kazakh cluster-A test, which DID close and was still refuted on sourcing — here the geometry doesn't even close). Diameters also differ across all three rows (1420/1220/700 mm), the classic signature of independently operated parallel strings in one corridor, not one pipe recorded three times.

rows.recommendation: No change. Treat as fully corroborated and structurally distinct from P0783 — retain as its own row. If anything, this cluster strengthens the case for leaving RouteAccuracy/route as-is (a 3-vertex schematic is appropriate for a well-documented but not finely mapped internal line).
rows.notes: uk.wikipedia 'Диканька — Кременчук — Кривий Ріг (газопровід)' (raw wikitext fetched directly): total length 272,2 км, projected throughput 3,2 млрд м³/рік, design pressure 5,5 МПа, built 1967–1968 — matches the sheet's 272.20 km / 3.20 bcm/y EXACTLY and predates P0783 by ~18-19 years, which alone rules out P1460 being a mislabeled duplicate of a line that didn't exist yet when it was built. Ownership split stated in the article: 180.2 km under UMG Cherkasytransgaz, 92 km under UMG Kharkivtransgas (pre-2020 operator naming; consistent with today's single state operator, Gas TSO of Ukraine). Diameter (700 mm, matching the sheet exactly) is NOT stated in the Wikipedia article text itself — flagging explicitly because an earlier AI-generated search summary asserted '700 mm' as if it were in the Wikipedia article, and it is not; I do not rely on that summary. Independent corroboration for diameter instead comes from OpenStreetMap way 807491112 (fetched directly via the OSM API, not the search summary): tags name='Диканька - Кременчук - Кривий Ріг', diameter='700', operator='Черкаситрансгаз', start_date='1968', substance='gas', usage='transmission' — i.e. a second, differently-sourced dataset agreeing on diameter, operator and build year. Both sources fetched directly (raw wikitext via action=raw; OSM via api.openstreetmap.org JSON), not taken from search-engine summaries, after the summary's diameter claim proved unverifiable in the primary text. All three URLs (both wiki articles + the OSM way) return HTTP 200 under `scripts/url_verifier.py`; the tool's fuzzy English-name match fails on all three because the page/way names are pure Cyrillic and the verifier does not transliterate — a documented false negative, not a dead-link signal.

rows.recommendation: No action from this cluster. P1485 (Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany) is the DOWNSTREAM continuation that P0783 feeds into per the uk.wikipedia Yelets-line article — this is corroborating context for cluster C's adjudication, not a new finding for cluster F. See kab_achb_evidence.md / cluster C for its own duplication question (P1485 vs P1481) and its separate Gazprom-ownership attribution flag, which is the same defect type raised on P0783 above.

open_questions: What is the correct territorial scope of P0783's stated 771.00 km — Yelets(Russia)-to-Kryvyi-Rih total, or Ukraine-territory-only? No source found states a length figure for this line at all; the sheet value is currently unverified in either direction.

Does P0783's Owner field attribute the WHOLE line to Gazprom PJSC, or already reflect a Russia/Ukraine split? The row summary supplied to this cluster says 'Owner includes Gazprom PJSC' without stating whether it is exclusive — if exclusive, this is an attribution defect of the same kind already flagged on P1485/cluster C, since the great majority of the corridor (Kremenchuk to Kryvyi Rih) is deep inside Ukraine and has been state-operated (Ukrtransgaz, then Gas TSO of Ukraine since 2020-01-01) throughout GEM's tracking period.

The 1400 mm (Wikipedia) vs 1420 mm (sheet) diameter reading for P0783 is treated here as consistent (1420 mm being the standard nominal Soviet large-diameter trunk class, of which 1400 mm is very likely an imprecise rounding in the Wikipedia prose) rather than a conflict — worth a one-line confirmation from a technical source if one surfaces, but not an escalation.
summary: THE HYPOTHESIS TESTED: that P0783 (Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 771.00 km / 1420 mm / 1986) and P1460 (Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 272.20 km / 700 mm) are the same physical corridor recorded twice, because both terminate at Kryvyi Rih and appear to share a 'Kremenchuk tail'. VERDICT: REFUTED, on sourcing and on independent structural evidence together. Fetching the raw uk.wikipedia article for the Dikanka line (not just a search-engine summary) found it to be a fully independent, separately named and separately sourced Soviet internal pipeline: built 1967-1968 (18-19 years before P0783 even existed), 272.2 km, 3.2 bcm/y design throughput, 5.5 MPa — matching the sheet's P1460 values on length and capacity EXACTLY. An OpenStreetMap way for the same corridor (fetched directly from the OSM API, independently of Wikipedia) supplies the diameter figure the Wikipedia article omits — 700 mm, again matching the sheet exactly — plus a matching operator and build year, giving genuine second-source agreement on the technical spec even though the Wikipedia text alone does not state diameter (an AI-generated search summary had wrongly implied it did; that claim is explicitly retracted here in favour of the primary-source finding). The Yelets line (P0783) is likewise independently documented: commissioned 1986 as part of the Siberia(Yamburg)-to-Balkans gas-supply project routed through a hub at Yelets in Russia's Lipetsk Oblast, 1400 mm diameter (reads as the standard 1420 mm Soviet trunk class), 7.5 MPa — a materially different pipe from P1460 on diameter, vintage, and stated purpose (transit corridor vs internal Ukrainian distribution trunk). The route-geometry test (already run in the main loop, route_geometry_findings.md finding F) independently corroborates the refutation from a structural angle: unlike the Kazakh cluster-A case where a suspected parent's route was the EXACT concatenation of two children's (and was STILL refuted on sourcing), here the concatenation test fails outright — 0 of P1460's 3 vertices and only 1 of P0775's 3 vertices fall within 0.5 km of P0783's own drawn trace, and all three rows carry different diameters (1420/1220/700 mm), the textbook signature of independently built and operated parallel strings sharing one corridor rather than one pipe triple-counted. The shared Dykanka and Kryvyi-Rih nodes are exactly that — shared NODES where genuinely distinct lines meet, hand off, or terminate, not evidence of shared PIPE; the Yelets-line article itself names Dykanka and the Kremenchuk-Ananiv handoff (P1485, cluster C) as its own downstream connections, independently reinforcing the same reading found in kab_achb_evidence.md. Two items survive as separate, narrower Update actions rather than as duplication findings: whether P0783's Owner field wrongly attributes the entire cross-border line to Gazprom PJSC (no source found supports Gazprom ownership of the Ukrainian majority of this corridor, and the Moldovan/Kazakh precedent in this project is that cross-border Soviet trunks get a jurisdictional OWNERSHIP split, not a single foreign owner), and whether the 771.00 km figure represents the whole Yelets-to-Kryvyi-Rih corridor or a Ukraine-only portion, since no source located here states a length figure for this line at all.
